rationale: Δppent is mechanically almost identical to (capx − dp) (net PPE change equals capex less depreciation and disposals), so this is a cosmetic re-specification of the archive's "Accrual Share of Net Investment" rather than a new mechanism.

The bounded share of asset growth going to noncash current assets is a genuine improvement over the archive's capex-denominated working-capital diversion measure (removing the small-denominator pathology), though it remains close to the standard Richardson-style ΔWC accrual component and so offers only moderate novelty.

The MIN-conjunction is a sensible construction and distinct from the archive entries, but inventory change is itself a component of total accruals, so the two legs are mechanically overlapping and the signal risks being a repackaging of the well-known inventory-growth and accrual anomalies.

The SIGN(oancf) term makes the spread essentially a negative-operating-cash-flow (distress/profitability) indicator scaled by capex, and it places high-capex/positive-OCF firms in the long leg, which directly contradicts the documented capex-underperformance direction the proposal otherwise relies on.

Substituting an external-financing channel for capex is a real economic change from "Accrual-Loaded Capex" and is grounded in the SEO earnings-management literature, but the short-leg/long-leg asymmetry is worrying since high-issuance/negative-accrual firms land in the predicted-high-return tail despite the issuance anomaly implying the opposite.

Moving from a level mix to a change-in-mix is a substantive rather than cosmetic variation on the archive's accrual-versus-capex family, though it is close to an equal-weighted difference of two individually known change signals and double-differencing accruals will add considerable noise.
